On primitive 3-generated axial algebras of Jordan type
Ilya Gorshkov and Alexey Staroletov∗
Abstract
Axial algebras of Jordan type η are commutative algebras generated by idempotents
whose adjoint operators have the minimal polynomial dividing (x −1)x(x −η), where
η ̸∈{0, 1} is ﬁxed, with restrictive multiplication rules. These properties generalize the
Pierce decompositions for idempotents in Jordan algebras, where 1
2 is replaced with η.
In particular, Jordan algebras generated by idempotents are axial algebras of Jordan
type 1
2. If η ̸= 1
2 then it is known that axial algebras of Jordan type η are factors of
the so-called Matsuo algebras corresponding to 3-transposition groups.
We call the generating idempotents axes and say that an axis is primitive if its
adjoint operator has 1-dimensional 1-eigenspace. It is known that a subalgebra gen-
erated by two primitive axes has dimension at most three. The 3-generated case has
been opened so far. We prove that any axial algebra of Jordan type generated by three
primitive axes has dimension at most nine. If the dimension is nine and η = 1
2 then
we either show how to ﬁnd a proper ideal in this algebra or prove that the algebra is
isomorphic to certain Jordan matrix algebras.

Introduction
The concept of axial algebras was introduced by Hall, Rehren, and Shpectorov [1]. These
algebras are commutative, nonassociative, and generated by idempotents. Axial algebras
extend the class of Majorana algebras which was introduced as a part of Majorana theory
by Ivanov [2]. The key motivational example for both theories is the Griess algebra, which
is a real commutative nonassociative algebra of dimension 196884 that has the Monster
sporadic simple group as its automorphism group. It is known that this algebra is generated
by idempotents that correspond to involutions from the conjugacy class 2A of the Monster.
Besides the class of Majorana algebras, axial algebras also include Jordan algebras generated
by idempotents and Matsuo algebras corresponding to 3-transposition groups. Thus, this
class provides a common approach for studying seemingly diﬀerent objects.
In this paper we focus on the class of axial algebras of Jordan type. Consider a ﬁeld F
and a commutative F-algebra A. If a ∈A then by ada we denote the right multiplication

Preliminaries
In this section we provide basic deﬁnitions, introduce notation, and describe properties of
axial algebras of Jordan type. Recall that we do not assume associativity of the product in
algebras.
2.1
Axial algebras of Jordan type and related objects
First, we recall the deﬁnition of Jordan algebras that are closely related to the objects
considered in this paper. We follow [6] on this topic. Throughout, we suppose that F is a
ﬁeld of characteristic not two.
Deﬁnition 1. A commutative F-algebra is called a Jordan algebra if its elements satisfy the
identity (x2y)x = x2(yx).

The class of axial algebras was introduced by Hall, Rehren, and Shpectorov [1]. These
algebras are commutative, nonassociative, and generated by idempotents with adjoint action
semi-simple. For more detailed information about this class one can see recent papers [7]

generated by a set of idempotents X such that for each a ∈X:
(1) the minimal ad-polynomial of a divides (x −1)x(x −η);
(2) the fusion rules for products of eigenvectors of ada are the following:

If a is a primitive axis of A, x ∈A, and y ∈A1(a) + A0(a) then a(xy) = (ax)y.

Frobenius form
It turned out that in the majority of known examples primitive axial algebras admit a bilinear
form that associates with the algebra product.
Deﬁnition 7. A non-zero bilinear form (·,·) on a commutative algebra A is called Frobenius
if the form associates with the algebra product, that is, (ab, c) = (a, bc) for all a, b, c ∈A.
In case of primitive axial algebras of Jordan type such a from can be deﬁned using the
projection map on 1-dimensional 1-eigenspaces of adjoint operators.
Deﬁnition 8. Suppose that a is a primitive axis of an axial algebra A. Then for every b ∈A
by ϕa(b) we denote the element of F such that the projection of b on A1(a) equals ϕa(b)a.
Now we are ready to formulate an important result stating that every primitive axial
algebra of Jordan type does admit a Frobenius form.
Lemma 2. [9, Theorem 4.1] Suppose that A be a primitive axial algebra of Jordan type η
generated by the set of primitive axes X. There exists a unique Frobenius bilinear form on
A such that
1. (a, u) = ϕa(u), for all a ∈X and all u ∈A;
2. (a, a) = 1, for all a ∈X;
3. (·,·) is invariant under automorphisms of A.
Moreover, this form is symmetric.

type with a given generating set, we assume that this form is from the conclusion of Lemma 2.

Ideals
To describe the variety of algebras, one needs to know how to ﬁnd the ideals in order to go
over to factor algebras. In this subsection we discuss ideals in axial algebras. Methods to
ﬁnd all ideals in an axial algebra A were developed in [7]. We adapted those results to axial
algebras of Jordan type.
Deﬁnition 9. Suppose that A is a primitive axial algebra of Jordan type and (·, ·) is the
Frobenius form as in Lemma 2. The projection graph ∆of A has as vertices all generating

elements of A with respect to this form, that is
A⊥= {u ∈A | (u, v) = 0 for all v ∈A}.
Recall that an algebra is simple if it contains no non-trivial ideals and the multiplication

Abstract: Axial algebras of Jordan type η are commutative algebras generated by idempotents whose adjoint operators have the minimal polynomial dividing (x −1)x(x −η), where η ̸∈{0, 1} is ﬁxed, with restrictive multiplication rules. These properties generalize the Pierce decompositions for idempotents in Jordan algebras, where 1 2 is replaced with η. In particular, Jordan algebras generated by idempotents are axial algebras of Jordan type 1 2. If η ̸= 1 2 then it is known that axial algebras of Jordan type η are factors of the so-called Matsuo algebras corresponding to 3-transposition groups. We call the generating idempotents axes and say that an axis is primitive if its adjoint operator has 1-dimensional 1-eigenspace. It is known that a subalgebra gen- erated by two primitive axes has dimension at most three. The 3-generated case has been opened so far. We prove that any axial algebra of Jordan type generated by three primitive axes has dimension at most nine. If the dimension is nine and η = 1 2 then we either show how to ﬁnd a proper ideal in this algebra or prove that the algebra is isomorphic to certain Jordan matrix algebras.
